requirements.summary: ESP-12F, AMS1117, Q1 (B/E/C), HLK-PM01 and relay pin assignments look plausible from the pin tables. However, relay-coil flyback diode D1 is wired backwards (anode on +5V, cathode on the transistor collector). J3 uses a 1x06 symbol on a 2x03 footprint, so physical pin numbering may not match. No local datasheet text was available to confirm the pinouts.

Boot straps are correct for ESP-12F normal boot. GPIO15 is pulled low by R5, GPIO2 is pulled high by R4, GPIO0 is pulled high by R3 with a button to GND, and EN and RST are pulled high by R1 and R2. The relay output on GPIO5 and the LED on GPIO4 are not strapping pins.

Rail budget looks adequate: the HLK-PM01 (5 V, 3 W) feeds the relay coil and an AMS1117-3.3 that powers the ESP-12F. No datasheet text is local to confirm ratings. The relay-coil flyback diode is reversed, which would short the 5V rail whenever Q1 turns on (see extra findings).

Varistor RV1 is a 07D221K, which is about 140 Vac rated (220 V varistor voltage). That is too low for 230 Vac mains: it will conduct continuously and overheat or fail. A 07D471K (about 300 Vac) is needed. The T500mA fuse F1 on the PSU branch is acceptable.
Resistor values are reasonable: the pull-ups are 10k, the LED resistors are 1k and 220R, and the base drive is 1k with a 10k pull-down. The varistor rating is wrong for mains (see MOD-PROT-001).

Relay K1 is a G5RL-1A-E but uses the Omron G2RL-1A-E footprint, which may not match its pin pitch. The ESP-12F uses the ESP-12E footprint (usually compatible). J3 has a 2x03 footprint against a 1x06 symbol. No datasheet is local to verify any of these.

extra_findings.text: error: Flyback diode D1 is reversed. Its anode is on +5V and its cathode is on the relay coil/Q1 collector node (/COIL_N). When Q1 turns on, D1 is forward biased and shorts +5V to GND, and the relay-coil kick is not clamped. The cathode must go to +5V and the anode to /COIL_N.
warning: J3 PROG exposes +5V (pin 2) while PS1 also drives +5V. Connecting a USB-serial adapter that supplies 5V at the same time would back-feed or contend with the HLK-PM01 output.
